statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in one of the official South African languages and must remain compliant with the Companies Regulations, 2011. Names must use Latin-alphabet characters, Arabic numerals, and certain permitted punctuation only; non-English names require an English translation (or transliteration) for CIPC examination and to ensure the name does not conflict with an existing mark or mislead the public.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tokens implying state, royal, or governmental patronage: 'President', 'Minister', 'Government', 'National', 'Municipal', 'Province', 'Public Service'
Tokens requiring regulatory authorization: 'Bank', 'Financial Services', 'Exchange', 'Trust', 'Insurance', 'Building Society'
Tokens implying a regulated legal, accounting, or auditing profession: 'Law', 'Attorney', 'Advocate', 'Accountant', 'Auditor', 'Notary'
Tokens falsely suggesting a public charitable or educational purpose: 'University', 'College', 'Foundation'
Tokens constituting an offensive, obscene, or contra bonos mores expression
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a request for reconsideration through the same CIPC e-Services transaction within 10 business days of rejection; if the matter is not resolved, an administrative review or formal application may be brought to the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. The appeal must be accompanied by a sworn affidavit and any evidence of prior trademark or name usage. CIPC will reinstate the reservation if the rejection is found to be erroneous. Applicable CIPC appeal fees and attorney drafting fees apply.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for low-risk administrative and mail-handling purposes only, provided the service supplies a registered physical street address in South Africa at which legal process and regulatory correspondence can be served during business hours. For an ISIC 7810 global EOR staffing agency conducting payroll activities, a virtual office is insufficient to satisfy the substance requirement and CIPC/SARS may challenge the arrangement if no operational management or payroll administration is carried out at a physical location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 15% unannounced inspection likelihood per calendar year for a newly incorporated Pty Ltd entity; the likelihood rises to 25% when aggregate payroll flows exceed ZAR 10 million or where the company provides contractor management services across multiple client sites, triggering enhanced SARS and Department of Employment and Labour oversight.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: South African Companies Act, 2008 (Act 71 of 2008) - Sections 13, 14, 15, 19, and 66
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) and Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; shares may be issued for such consideration as determined by the Board. No escrow account requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company adopts its Memorandum of Incorporation and registers as a Proprietary Limited Company under the South African Companies Act 71 of 2008. FURTHER RESOLVED that the subscribers accept the allotment and issue of 100 ordinary shares of ZAR 1.00 each, fully paid in cash, and that the registered office be established at the address set out in the Notice of Incorporation within the Republic of South Africa. FURTHER RESOLVED that the named individuals be and are hereby appointed as Director, Company Secretary, and Financial Officer respectively, each with full authority to open corporate bank accounts, execute the Notice of Incorporation, and file all statutory returns with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission. THIS RESOLUTION shall take effect immediately upon signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search through the CIPC e-Services portal. Reserve the proposed company name for a validity period of 12 months (extendable to 24 months with a licence-dependent name) and pay the prescribed name reservation fee. Obtain the provisional reservation reference number.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in the required format
Director and subscriber certified identity documents
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is objected to or rejected, submit an alternative name or file a reconsideration request with CIPC within 20 business days using the prescribed objection/reconsideration procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum of Incorporation and Incorporation Forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised Legal Representative / CIPC Registered Business Practitioner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) containing the company's constitution, share structure, and director powers. Complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation), Form CoR 14.1A (Consent to Act as Director), and Form CoR 14.2 (Appointment of Auditors/Company Secretary as applicable). Verify the registered office address and ensure all signatories execute the documents before a commissioner of oaths.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of director and subscriber identity documents
Proof of physical registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any defective or inconsistent clauses and re-execute the MOI; resubmit the corrected filing to CIPC within the statutory 20-business-day correction window without additional penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement of Incorporation Application with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services Portal / CIPC Customer Contact Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the complete incorporation application via CIPC e-Services together with the prescribed incorporation fee (approximately ZAR 175). Retain the CIPC application transaction reference number for tracking. Verify that all mandatory fields are populated to avoid validation errors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises a query or deficiency notice, respond with the required corrections within 20 business days. Unresolved applications may be resubmitted with a fresh application fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download and verify the electronic Certificate of Incorporation once CIPC approves the application. Confirm the company registration number, incorporation date, company name, and standard company type. Retain the certificate as the primary corporate status document for all downstream registrations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains incorrect details, apply for a correction of registration particulars via CIPC using the prescribed form and pay the applicable amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); Department of Employment and Labour (UIF/COIDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with SARS for Income Tax, withholds (PAYE), and Value-Added Tax (if turnover exceeds the VAT threshold). Register with the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and the Compensation Fund (COIDA). Submit the registration pack electronically or at the applicable SARS and Department of Employment and Labour offices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS or DEL queries the registration, resubmit the supporting documents with an explanatory letter via the SARS branch resolution desk or DEL regional office; escalating internally for a senior case officer review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Private Employment Agency Registration Certificate (issued under the Employment Services Act, No. 4 of 2014)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Targeted registration only; office-based EOR and payroll activities do not trigger Listing Notices 1, 2, or 3 of the 2014 EIA Regulations (as amended).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with SANS 10400 building ventilation and energy efficiency requirements; negligible wastewater discharge; general waste separation and disposal in accordance with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, No. 59 of 2008; no VOC or industrial emission thresholds applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and emergency evacuation certification from the local municipal Fire and Rescue Service; electrical certificate of compliance; structural load inspection certificate; and Risk Assessment and Workplace Clearance Certificate issued under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, No. 85 of 1993.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); electronic filing, registration and compliance via the SARS eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za) and SARS branch network.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned South African Proprietary Limited company must obtain a SARS income tax reference number by registering on eFiling (or at a SARS branch) using: the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) registration certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, certified IDs of directors/shareholders, the company's banking details, and the appointment of a resident public officer. The company should also register for VAT, PAYE, UIF, and SDL if applicable. Foreign shareholders must submit the relevant SARS non-resident declarations and supporting incorporation documents. SARS issues a tax reference number and tax compliance status pin automatically through eFiling after verification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (South African resident company subject to normal income tax on worldwide taxable income, with no general pass-through regime; a (Pty) Ltd is a separate taxable person for income tax and VAT purposes).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under South African law. A (Pty) Ltd is automatically taxed as a company. Available statutory elections include election under section 12E for taxation as a Small Business Corporation (reduced graduated rates, subject to shareholder and revenue limits), VAT group registration election under the VAT Act (where two or more resident companies are under common control), voluntary VAT registration for taxable supplies above ZAR 50,000, apportionment/input tax election for partially taxable suppliers, and the election to account for VAT on the payments basis for vendors with qualifying turnover.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration at ZAR 1,000,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period (or where it will be exceeded in the next 30 days); voluntary registration at ZAR 50,000 of taxable supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, central invoice stamping, or government API clearance for VAT invoices. Electronic tax invoices are permitted provided they comply with section 20 of the VAT Act (all prescribed particulars, issuance within 21 days of supply, and adequate data integrity controls). SARS eFiling and SARS API integration are used for filing VAT returns and data exchange, but there is no mandatory country-specific clearance API for business-to-business electronic invoices at this stage.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exported goods where the supplier exports the goods by the due date for the VAT return, or supplies services to a non-resident person who is not in South Africa at the time the services are rendered and the services are physically rendered outside South Africa. For an EOR/staffing payroll business providing administrative and payroll services to foreign clients, zero-rating is available if the services are supplied to and consumed by non-residents outside South Africa and supporting documentary evidence is retained. Temporary VAT zero-rating rules also apply to movable goods supplied to recipients outside South Africa where the goods are exported under customs procedures.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500) / bill of entry with customs clearing number
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / travel document proving physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank SWIFT confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may claw back zero-rated input VAT and impose additional output tax where export documentation is deficient, where goods or services are not genuinely exported, or where the supplier fails to prove delivery into an export destination. Under the Tax Administration Act, understatement penalties range from 10% to 75% of the shortfall depending on conduct, plus interest at the prescribed rate. Fraudulent zero-rating claims, false customs declarations, or deliberate non-repatriation of export proceeds may attract criminal prosecution, hefty fines, and imprisonment of up to five years, in addition to full VAT recovery and disqualification from VAT registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv, formerly the Exchange Control Department), pursuant to the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations of 1961. FinSurv exercises delegated exchange-control authority through Authorized Dealers, being the domestic commercial banks licensed to transact foreign exchange, and coordinates enforcement with the South African Revenue Service (SARS) through tax-clearance and balance-of-payments reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa accepts IMF Article VIII obligations, so current-account transactions are freely convertible without SARB approval; cross-border EOR service fees, contractor salaries, and operational service payments may be settled in any permitted foreign currency and remitted through an Authorized Dealer on submission of bona fide supporting documentation. The capital account remains subject to a managed regime: inward equity investment, share transfers to non-residents, and external shareholder loans require Authorized Dealer registration, use of prescribed capital purpose codes, and, in the case of external loans above ZAR 50 million or structurally complex inward/outward investments, prior FinSurv approval. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is lawful but practically gated by: (i) a valid SARS Tax Clearance Certificate in respect of the remitting company and the non-resident beneficial owner; (ii) audited annual financial statements or an Authorized Dealer designatory certificate confirming sufficient distributable reserves; (iii) a board resolution declaring the dividend; (iv) proof of dividends tax at 15%, or a treaty-reduced rate where applicable; and (v) the dealer's foreign-exchange reporting return. The South African rand is a freely floating currency with no exchange-rate bands or rationing; the main compliance risk for a global EOR platform is mischaracterizing equity injections as current-account payments, which triggers FinSurv verification, documentary penalties, and suspension of the dealer's delegated authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual, the EOR platform's cross-border client fees constitute an export of services for exchange-control purposes. All export proceeds must be repatriated to South Africa through an Authorized Dealer within 180 days from the date of the invoice or, if earlier, the date the services are rendered. The historical mandatory surrender ratio was abolished in the 2010 liberalization, so there is no compulsory conversion percentage: the exporter may retain 100% of service proceeds in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) with a South African Authorized Dealer or, upon concession, in an approved offshore account; any elective conversion into rand must be executed through an Authorized Dealer at the prevailing market rate. Export receipts must be reported to FinSurv through the dealer's ongoing balance-of-payments submissions and, when retained in an FCA, through monthly aggregated reporting. Non-repatriation within the 180-day period or unauthorized offshore retention is an exchange-control violation exposing the entity to administrative penalties, increased monitoring, revocation of trade facilities, and potential criminal liability, making periodic cash-flow reconciliation of invoices received against incoming SWIFT credits a mandatory treasury control.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited (Standard Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: ZAR Operational Business Account coupled with a USD/EUR/GBP Foreign Currency Account (FCA), plus a ring-fenced client-money payroll settlement sub-account enabling segregated custody of EOR client float funds

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: FirstRand Bank Limited, acting through First National Bank (FNB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Premium Plus Current Account with an integrated FNB Global Account / FCA and a mass-payment API rail purpose-built for batched international contractor disbursements

ZAR Business Current Account paired with a Trade and Working Capital FX facility, a linked Foreign Currency Account, and an escrow-style Conditional Payment Account for isolating the employer-of-record payroll float
BusinessEvolve ZAR Current Account with simultaneously opened USD/EUR FCA and a treasury electronic dealing platform for same-day spot execution and forward bookings

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: CONDITIONALLY VIABLE strictly as an execution layer, never as the sole banking rail for the South African resident entity. Wise operates in South Africa through a registered local entity licensed as an authorized financial services provider under FSCA oversight and offers efficient contractor payments into more than 40 jurisdictions; however, all incoming ZAR or hard-currency settlement of international EOR receivables must first clear through a SARB-licensed Authorized Dealer because an offshore digital EMI cannot maintain a ZAR IBAN, lawfully perform ZAR conversions, or discharge the company's FinSurv export-proceeds reporting obligations without a local banking partner. The optimal Treasury architecture is: receive client fees into a Tier-1 Authorized Dealer current account or FCA; retain the proportion payable to South African contractors for execution through the local payroll direct-debit and ACB rail; and transmit the offshore proportion through Wise or a similarly licensed payment aggregator such as Convera or Corpay, with each batch covered by a pre-approved standing mandate and a machine-readable payroll ledger. Offshore-only EMIs domiciled in the EU or UK with no FSCA authorization cannot lawfully solicit South African corporate clients and will be rejected by local Authorized Dealers for SARB reporting, thereby rendering pure-offshore EMI configuration non-viable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one executive officer, being the CEO or CFO and preferably a South African resident director, must appear in person before a bank official to sign the corporate banking mandate under FICA section 21 identification requirements. Where the signatory is a non-resident director, banks will accept either a visit to a South African branch or, on concession, a supervised live video interview with the bank officer plus notarized and apostilled passport copies, bank-certified address proof, and a certified board resolution conferring signing authority. FNB and Standard Bank permit fully remote onboarding only when the ultimate beneficial owner structure is transparent, the company's CIPC filings are clean and current, and the foreign parent resides in a FATF-equivalent jurisdiction; even then, the bank reserves the right to require a physical mandate-signing session for the first signatory. All directors, all natural persons holding 25% or more of the shares or voting rights (UBOs), and the company secretary must be disclosed in the bank's UBO register, and the non-resident UBO must, regardless of residence, be identifiable through acceptable KYC documentation; omission of a single beneficial owner typically delays account activation by four to eight weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through or sweep payroll pattern: the company receives large lump-sum EOR client fees from foreign jurisdictions and disperses 70 to 85 percent onward to a high-volume network of individual foreign contractors within 24 to 72 hours, which mimics money-laundering layering and triggers automated transaction-monitoring alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete defense bundle comprising: the signed global EOR service agreement with the foreign end-client; a line-item payroll settlement ledger per contractor segregating salary, tax, social contributions, and platform margin; monthly payslips and contractor engagement agreements; the inbound SWIFT MT103 records identifying the remitting client and source account; a written Treasury policy explaining the contractual payroll float; and a SARS-compliant payroll register evidencing that the entity withholds and remits all South African statutory payroll deductions for locally engaged staff, thereby proving a substantive economic business rather than a financial relay.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to contractors in high-risk or FATF-grey-listed jurisdictions, and to foreign nationals whose address verification is weak, raising sanctions or terrorist-financing concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A jurisdiction-risk matrix classifying each payment corridor under FATF and SARB guidance; a full contractor KYC file per offshore beneficiary comprising government-issued identification, proof of residential address, signed contractor agreement, and independent verification of professional status; sanctions and PEP screening outputs with false-positive resolution notes; and a legal opinion confirming that the employer-of-record model validly designates the South African entity as the contractual principal of the offshore contractor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, small-value outbound foreign-exchange transactions executed as numerous MT103s to payroll aggregators without a standing instruction, which may be interpreted as structuring designed to circumvent dealer approval thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A bank-approved standing payment mandate for international mass payroll; an aggregated batch file for each pay run; a published payroll calendar; Authorized Dealer FX tickets confirming that every conversion was executed at market rates through the bank's dealing desk; and a quarterly CFO-certified reconciliation memorandum reconciling batch totals to the underlying contractor settlement ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder loan advances or equity injections that could be characterized as unauthorized external loans, round-tripping, or prohibited loop-structure funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For equity: the share subscription agreement, a Companies Act section 40 board resolution authorizing the issue, the CIPC share register extract, and the prescribed FinSurv non-resident capital declaration / inward FDI notification filed by the Authorized Dealer. For loan capital: the executed external loan agreement, the prescribed external-loan registration return, a FinSurv approval letter where the principal exceeds ZAR 50 million, and a source-of-funds certificate issued by the remitting foreign bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the EOR client invoice value received and the actual aggregated contractor settlements paid, producing profitability distortion alerts and potential invoice-discounting concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A monthly margin and netting worksheet per EOR client; the tax-compliant invoice issued to the client under the VAT Act (including the VAT treatment of the platform fee); individual contractor settlement advices; bank ledger extracts for each pay run; and a signed management representation letter explaining gross margin, foreign withholding tax set-offs, payroll float residuals, and timing differences between cash receipt and pay-run execution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial capitalization of the proprietary limited company, the compliant routing is a SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 equivalent) transfer denominated in ZAR, USD, EUR, or GBP from the foreign shareholder's bank to the company's account held at a South African Authorized Dealer. The remittance must reference the standard SARB purpose code for inward direct investment in equity capital, the receiving bank records the transaction on its balance-of-payments return as an equity contribution, and the company must provide the prescribed FinSurv non-resident declaration, its CIPC certificate, the share register extract, the board resolution approving the share issue, and the completed FICA corporate file. Proceeds are initially placed in an inward-funding suspense account and released to the operational ZAR account or the Foreign Currency Account after verification, normally within one to three business days. Subsequent working-capital injections from non-resident shareholders must follow either: a formal subordinated shareholder loan registered with the Authorized Dealer and, where the principal exceeds ZAR 50 million, approved in advance by FinSurv; or a documented intercompany settlement in respect of actual services rendered. A prohibited loop structure arises if foreign EOR fee income is routed offshore and re-injected into South Africa as equity or subordinated debt without a genuine business purpose, and FinSurv will require demonstrable use of funds, source-of-wealth evidence, and transactional flow charts before accepting the second injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the EOR contractor payroll and ancillary trade follow a layered clearing-rail hierarchy: (i) Local payroll rail: South African contractors are paid through the national real-time clearing and settlement system (SAMOS/RTCS) and the Automated Clearing Bureau (ACB) using a local payroll direct-debit or direct-credit code with full PAYE/UIF/SDL reconciliation; (ii) Cross-border mass payroll rail: salaries to offshore contractors are executed as aggregated SWIFT MT103 batches through the Authorized Dealer's international mass-payment platform (such as FNB Global, Standard Bank International e-Channel, or Absa Global Access) or through licensed aggregators including Wise Business, Convera, and Corpay, which localize funds into beneficiary bank accounts by RTGS or ACH in the contractor's jurisdiction; (iii) Trade settlement rail: where the employer-of-record model additionally procures hardware, equipment, or employee benefits in kind, documentary collections and confirmed or unconfirmed Commercial Letters of Credit are permitted only when underpinned by purchase contracts, transport documents, and customs entries, with payment released on complying presentation; and (iv) Statutory outbound rail: foreign withholding taxes, VAT, and payroll statutory deductions are settled through SARS eFiling using the South African banking rails. Every outward contractor payment requires the Authorized Dealer to hold a valid SARS Tax Clearance Certificate for the remitting company, the underlying contractor invoice or settlement advice, the payroll register, and, for cumulative annual remittances above the dealer's delegated limits, a prescribed outward-payment return to FinSurv containing the purpose code for remuneration for services rendered by non-resident independent contractors.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Confirmed Forward Exchange Contracts (FECs) with a South African Authorized Dealer, available for terms up to 12 months and covering known or anticipated net foreign-currency receivables and payroll liabilities, each contract supported by documentary evidence of the underlying EOR client contract and payroll forecast.

Rolling Forward Exchange Contracts, automatically renewed on maturity, permitted where the underlying cross-border service exposure remains outstanding and is re-verified by the dealer on a quarterly basis.

Currency Options, including vanilla puts and calls and zero-cost collars, transacted with an Authorized Dealer under a board-approved hedging mandate referencing the platform's projected USD/ZAR, EUR/ZAR, and GBP/ZAR exposures derived from the EOR receivable pipeline.

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS), permitted with prior FinSurv approval where the entity holds a substantial foreign-currency-denominated shareholder loan, acquisition debt, or offshore financial asset requiring matched funding and ongoing interest and principal servicing.

Onshore OTC Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in USD/ZAR, phased in by the SARB and National Treasury following the 2023 liquidity-market reform, executed exclusively through an Authorized Dealer and requiring demonstration of actual ZAR exposure arising from EOR fee inflows plus full FinSurv transaction reporting and ZAR settlement without physical delivery.

Natural hedging through the Foreign Currency Account (FCA) structure, under which matched foreign-currency assets (invoiced receivables retained in the FCA) are applied directly against foreign-currency liabilities (offshore contractor payroll obligations), thereby minimizing reliance on derivative instruments and reducing transaction costs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC imposes a late-filing penalty and suspension of good standing; failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years triggers a CIPC deregistration notice and administrative strike-off under Companies Act s 82.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual return; any change in beneficial ownership, including a shareholding transfer, must be reported within 7 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the beneficial ownership return is an offence under the Companies Act and may result in fines, imprisonment, rejection of the annual return, and a compliance notice from CIPC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (filing requirement where public interest score is at least 350)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepared within 6 months after financial year-end; filed with CIPC within the prescribed period when the public interest score threshold applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file audited annual financial statements when required is a breach of the Companies Act and may lead to a CIPC compliance notice, referral to enforcement authorities, and director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit where the public interest score equals or exceeds 350, or where the MOI or shareholders' agreement requires audit; independent review required for a public interest score between 100 and 349; compiled financial statements may be prepared for a public interest score below 100. The public interest score is calculated under the Companies Regulations, including points for employees, turnover, third-party liabilities, and number of shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or IFRS for SMEs as adopted by the Financial Reporting Standards Council (FRSC); South African GAAP is not applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a beneficial ownership register and file the annual CIPC beneficial ownership confirmation with the annual return. Any shareholding transfer or indirect change of control must be recorded in the register and reported to CIPC within 7 days, without waiting for the annual cycle.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 20,000 per annum for a full audit, depending on payroll volume and group complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; (28% for prior years; small business corporation turnover-based graduated rate 0%-21% if the (Pty) Ltd qualifies with annual turnover below ZAR 20 million and meets the SBC definition in s12E).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Employment Tax Incentive (ETI) for qualifying employees aged 18-29; s11D research and development 150% deduction; s12H learnership allowance (ZAR 40,000 per qualifying learner per year); s12B accelerated capital allowance (125%) for qualifying renewable-energy and energy-efficiency assets used in the EOR payroll infrastructure; s12C wear-and-tear on computers/ERP systems; no special EOR-specific payroll deduction beyond normal s11(a) expenditure that is actually incurred and not of a capital nature.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return for companies, including Pty Ltd) filed exclusively through the SARS eFiling platform at www.sarsefiling.co.za; provisional tax returns via IRP6; standard-risk companies may receive an Auto-Assessment from SARS requiring confirmation or adjustment within 40 business days.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual ITR14 return plus two mandatory provisional (IRP6) payments per year (first on the last day of the sixth month of the year of assessment, second on the last day of the year of assessment) and an optional top-up provisional payment six months after year-end; monthly PAYE, UIF, and SDL returns and payments for an employer of record.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: ITR14 due within 12 months of the financial year-end (a February year-end company must file by the end of January of the following year under SARS practice); the final provisional top-up payment for a February year-end is due by the last day of September following the year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Withholding Taxes Declared (PAYE / DWT / Interest / Royalty)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The employer of record must declare employees' tax (PAYE) deducted under the 4th Schedule and any dividends withholding tax (20%) on distributions declared to shareholders, including non-resident beneficial owners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners claiming DTA relief must file the SARS DWT declaration and provide a residence certificate via eFiling within the prescribed 18-month period for refund/relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to submit: fixed-amount penalty of up to ZAR 16,000 per month for large businesses (ZAR 250-500 for smaller taxpayers) and lesser per-referral penalties, plus interest at the prescribed rate (repo + 3%) compounded on unpaid tax; understatement penalty under s222 TAA of up to 150% of the shortfall (200% for withholding-tax shortfalls) depending on behavior: standard 0%, substantial understatement 25%, failure to take reasonable care 50%, no reasonable grounds 75%, gross negligence 100%, intentional tax evasion 150%; criminal prosecution under s235 TAA may add a fine of up to ZAR 100,000 (or ZAR 250,000 on repeat offence) and imprisonment of up to five years (up to ten years for failure to pay over tax collected).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (s64E Income Tax Act 58 of 1962) on dividends paid or declared by the South African (Pty) Ltd, calculated on the amount actually paid without set-off; exemption applies to dividends paid to resident companies exempt under s10(1)(k), the SA Government, a SA branch of a foreign company holding the shares as trading assets, and certain public benefit/retirement vehicles; international treaty rates commonly reduce the 20% rate to 5%-15% depending on shareholding (e.g., 5% for shareholdings of at least 10% under the SA-US, SA-UK, and SA-Mauritius DTAs, 10%-15% for portfolio holdings).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must secure a treaty relief in two stages: (1) before payment, submit a signed SARS 'Declaration by Beneficial Owner of Dividends/Interest/Royalties' setting out treaty benefits, together with a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the relevant DTA jurisdiction and proof of beneficial ownership; (2) where the statutory 20%/15% rate was already withheld, the foreign recipient, not the local company, applies on eFiling (IT-DWT/IT(WHT) forms) for a refund of the excess within three years of payment, annexing the TRC and source documentation; SARS may require a detailed OECD-style LOB analysis before issuing a directive, and advance treaty-rate rulings are available through the International Tax Rulings division.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax of 15% on interest paid to non-residents (s50B) and 15% on royalties (s51B); DTA-reduced rates commonly 0%-15% (e.g., 0% or 5% on interest under certain African and European DTAs; 5%-10% on royalties under the SA-UK and SA-US DTAs where the beneficial owner is not an agent/paper bridge).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: South Africa uses no statutory de minimis turnover or related-party threshold that automatically triggers the Local File or Master File; SARS adopts the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and expects contemporaneous arm's-length documentation for any cross-border connected-person transaction, including EOR service fees, payroll reimbursements, software royalties, and management charges; a full Local File (s31 TP policy, functional analysis, benchmarking study) is the prudent default for a global EOR operating on cross-border payroll rails and is specifically reviewed under SARS TP Practice Note 7 and the Transactional Net Margin Method; the Global Minimum Tax Act 2024 (effective for years commencing on or after 31 December 2024) imposes a 15% minimum top-up tax (IIR/UTPR) only on MNE groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more, but the SARS TP documentation expectation remains applicable to all connected cross-border dealings.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa has no Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, but substantive tests arise through four overlapping doctrines: (i) the s31 transfer-pricing rule requires the SA EOR to demonstrate real functions, assets, and risks and prevents pricing that reflects artificial allocation of profit offshore; (ii) the general anti-avoidance rules (s80A-s80L) recharacterize impermissible avoidance arrangements lacking commercial substance, including circular payroll flows and conduit interposed entities; (iii) the CFC regime (s9D) attributes undistributed foreign passive income of a controlled foreign company to the South African shareholder; (iv) the GAAR/domestic-law PE definition may be triggered if the SA company claims to be an independent 'employer of record' but in substance merely routes funds from a foreign principal to SA workers without assuming payroll, SACU, and dismissal risk. Directors must maintain board minutes, payroll contracts, and bank statements proving that the (Pty) Ltd genuinely employs the workforce, processes PAYE/UIF/SDL, and retains employment-law liability in South Africa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting EOR service fees, under-declaring gross payroll/commission, inflating or fabricating payroll deductions, backdating employment contracts, destroying payroll records, or colluding with a foreign contractor to reclassify employees as independent contractors while the company holds employer-of-record duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS understatement penalty under s222/s223 TAA of up to 150% of the shortfall (up to 200% for withholding taxes) plus interest at the prescribed rate; criminal conviction under s235 TAA attracts a fine of up to ZAR 100,000 and imprisonment of up to five years, and up to ZAR 250,000 and ten years on a subsequent or aggravated offence; the tax debt is not discharged by criminal punishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under s160 and s162 TAA the SARS has a statutory right to recover unpaid company taxes (PAYE, VAT, provisional tax) from the director who is a 'representative taxpayer' if the failure is due to negligence or fraud, without proof of misconduct beyond knowledge of the deficiency; SARS may issue a s194 travel ban (blocking certificate), attach personal bank accounts, and institute civil sequestration proceedings; directors who sign false returns are individually criminally liable up to ten years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the (Pty) Ltd as a pure paper conduit for cross-border payroll and intercompany fees with no physical office, no SA-resident directors, no payroll administration, no bank account in its own name, or with contracts that transfer all risk back to a foreign EOR principal; circular fund flows or reimbursement without a real mark-up; purposefully claiming DTA benefits while having no PE/management in South Africa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS recharacterizes or disregards the arrangement under s80C-s80D (GAAR), adjusts the consideration to an arm's-length amount under s31, and imposes an understatement penalty of 75%-150% for 'no reasonable grounds' or 'intentional evasion' plus interest; under the CFC rules (s9D) foreign dividends or passive income may be attributed and taxed in SA at 27%; a shell with a 100% foreign parent may also trigger the new Global Minimum Tax (15%) if the group is within the EUR 750 million threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: SARS may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable for the whole deficient tax plus penalties under s160 TAA; the court may issue a conservation order over personal assets, SARS may apply to liquidate the company (which voids all benefit of the arrangement), and directors risk an arrest warrant for criminal tax fraud (s235 TAA) as the arrangement is treated as a deliberate scheme to evade tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unpaid or Diverted Payroll Taxes (PAYE/UIF/SDL) and Employee Trust Monies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deducting employees' tax from salaries and then failing to remit the amounts to SARS on the due date, using PAYE collections for operating expenses or foreign FX transfers via Wise, under-declaring the remuneration paid to global EOR workers, or failing to register for PAYE/UIF/SDL as an employer of record.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS imposes 10%-plus prescribed interest on the outstanding amount, a 200% understatement penalty on the withheld-tax shortfall, and fixed monthly penalties for late returns; s236 TAA makes the deliberate failure to pay over tax a criminal offence punishable by a fine and imprisonment of up to ten years; SARS issues a s164 summons and a s169 estimate of assessment based on payroll records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are automatically jointly and severally liable under s160 TAA as representative taxpayers for all unremitted PAYE/UIF/SDL; SARS may attach a director's personal pension, overseas property, and personal credit position without first exhausting civil recovery against the company; a travel ban is typically imposed before the start of an audit or criminal prosecution, and directors face disqualification from acting as company directors under the South African Companies Act 71 of 2008 after conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the EOR payroll platform to blend, split, or route funds on behalf of undisclosed overseas principals with no verifiable source-of-funds due diligence, failing to register and file beneficial-ownership information with the CIPC under the General Laws Amendment Act 2022, or processing payroll for a sanctioned person or entity on the UN/SARS sanctions lists through the EOR rails (including via Wise or local direct debit).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) may impose administrative penalties of up to ZAR 10 million per contravention of the FIC Act (and up to ZAR 50 million in aggravated categories) plus daily penalties; a South African court may order disgorgement of the entire payroll flow; under POCA the laundering of proceeds is punishable by imprisonment of up to 15 years and a fine of up to ZAR 100 million; the company faces seizure of all funds in the payroll bank account and denial of the banking licence for its payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the AML Compliance Officer are personally liable for FIC Act penalties where the failure is attributable to their gross negligence; courts may issue a personal forfeiture order over assets linked to the laundered payroll; directors face criminal prosecution under POCA and the FIC Act with prison terms of up to 15 years, and the beneficial-ownership register mismatch is a separate criminal offence carrying imprisonment (up to 10 years under the Companies Act as amended) plus a personal fine; the FIC may also obtain a travel ban against the director pending investigation.
